help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How to dictate, which modes there are, and what to do if something doesn't work.

hotkeys.holdText: Short presses and combos like Ctrl+C don't start dictation.
hotkeys.handsFreeText: Double-press and recording runs on its own; press once more to stop.
hotkeys.broadcastText: The text is typed into each selected open RDP window in turn, then focus comes back.
hotkeys.commandText: Edits the selected text with a voice command, using AI.
hotkeys.cancelText: Discards the current recording, so nothing gets inserted.
hotkeys.insertLastText: Insert the last transcribed text again — for example, if it went to the wrong window.

modes.auto: Rupor recognizes RDP windows on its own and types into them; everywhere else it pastes via the clipboard.
modes.type: SendInput, one character at a time: any alphabet and emoji with any keyboard layout, works in RDP with the clipboard disabled.
modes.clipboard: The fastest option for long text. Your clipboard is restored after pasting.
modes.broadcast: Rupor activates each selected RDP window, types the text and returns focus to where you were.

help.commandText: Select text in any window, hold the shortcut and say what to do with it. Rupor replaces the selection with the result. Requires AI cleanup to be on.

faq.adminQ: Text isn't inserted into a window running as administrator
faq.adminA: Windows doesn't let regular programs type into elevated windows (like Registry Editor or Task Manager). Rupor shows a warning with a “Restart as administrator” button — after the restart, inserting works.
faq.rdpQ: The shortcut doesn't work in full-screen RDP
faq.rdpA: Rupor uses a low-level keyboard hook and sees keys even in a full-screen session. If it still doesn't fire, make sure mstsc's “Local Resources → Keyboard” isn't set to “On the remote computer” for Windows key combinations — or pick another key (like F13 or Pause).
faq.cudaQ: Recognition is slow, or there's a CUDA error
faq.cudaA: Make sure you have an NVIDIA driver with CUDA 12 support (528 or newer; the latest is best) and that the CUDA libraries are downloaded (Settings → About → Setup wizard). On a CUDA error Rupor switches to the CPU (int8) automatically and tells you — it's slower, but it works.
faq.micA: Open Settings → Dictation and pick a microphone — the level meter should move when you speak. Make sure microphone access is allowed in Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone.
faq.aiQ: AI doesn't respond or takes too long
faq.aiA: Click “Check” in the AI settings — Rupor shows your balance, or the error if the key doesn't work. Try Amazon Bedrock as the preferred OpenRouter provider. If AI doesn't reply within the timeout, the raw text is inserted — nothing is lost.
faq.ctrlQ: My Ctrl+Win shortcuts (like Ctrl+Win+D) stopped working
faq.ctrlA: Rupor doesn't block them: if you press another key while holding Ctrl+Win, recording is quietly canceled and the shortcut works as usual. Presses shorter than 0.25 s don't start dictation.
faq.rdpTargetsQ: A broadcast didn't reach an RDP session
faq.rdpTargetsA: Text is broadcast only to open, selected sessions: Settings → Insertion → Broadcast sessions, or “Broadcast to RDP” in the tray menu. A session is remembered by the server name in the window title. If none is selected, nothing is broadcast — you can still insert the text with “Paste last”.
faq.learnQ: The dictionary added a word by itself
faq.learnA: That was your correction: after the text was inserted you fixed a word, and Rupor remembered it to get it right next time. If that was a mistake, click Undo in the indicator or delete the term on the Dictionary page. You can also switch to “Ask first” or turn learning off there.
faq.duckQ: Music gets quieter when I dictate
faq.duckA: That's by design: while recording, Rupor lowers other apps' audio — music, videos, calls — and restores the previous volume when recording ends. Choose how much to lower it, or turn it off, in Settings → Dictation → Computer audio while recording. If Rupor closes mid-recording, the volume is restored the next time it starts.

vocab.subtitle: Rupor primes speech recognition with the words you say often — names and terms come out right without a hand-made dictionary.
